refuseKillObservation: When ProcessManager passes it: `closeTreeLocked` (root only; workers in the same close go through `stopProcessSerialized(token, locator, treeStopTimeoutMs)` with NO options), `removeTreeProcess` (root resurrection), and `controllerAlive` -- in each case exactly when the caller's own `runtime.probe` returned `not-recorded-process`, and never from `retireWorkerLocator` (markWorkerDeadLocked / retireUnconfirmedBoot / launchWorker), which calls `stopProcess(token, locator, workerStopTimeoutMs)` with no options. For the tmux runtime the flag is REDUNDANT as a safety mechanism: `TmuxRuntime.stop` (runtime-tmux.ts l.483-492) checks `options.refuseKill` immediately before its own `verifyPaneProcess` gate, and that gate would return the same non-verified verdict for the same locator moments later and refuse the kill itself -- the driver's negative control shows exactly that (stale locator, skipGraceful only, no refuseKill -> no kill-pane, one refusal log line). What refuseKill buys on tmux is (a) one fewer list-panes + /proc round trip and (b) one log line per decision instead of two (the caller's `treating ... as dead: <detail>` plus the runtime's `not killing pane ...`), which is the collapse the reviewer's non-blocking r3997829569 asked for. For a runtime without its own identity gate (FakeRuntime today; a real kubernetes runtime later if its `stop` cannot re-verify pod identity cheaply) the flag is the ONLY thing standing between the caller's verdict and the destroy step: FakeRuntime.stop's `destroyed = !refuseKill && !strangers.has(uid) && processes.has(uid)` relies on `strangers` rather than the flag for the occupied case, so even there the flag is belt-and-braces. Net: necessary for the interface contract (a Runtime is not required to re-verify at kill time -- the contract row 'stop with refuseKill asks the process to exit but never destroys it' holds over both runtimes), redundant for TmuxRuntime's correctness, and the one place a tmux stop can skip the kill without re-verifying is guarded by the caller having JUST verified the same locator. Risk to note for the reviewer: `refuseKill` is decided from a probe taken before the graceful branch; if the recorded process were to become the pane's process again between probe and kill (not possible on tmux -- a pane's root pid never changes), refuseKill would skip a kill the gate would have allowed. No change recommended.
